Title: Perception of Upright: Multisensory Convergence and the Role of Temporo-Parietal Cortex
Abstract: He proposed that the brain implements a computational strategy based on an internal bias signal to correct for the noisy inputs from the <m>otolith</m> organs (Figure 4). This internal signal, referred to as "the <m>idiotropic</m> <m>vector</m>," is a constant, body-fixed <m>vector</m> that is added to the estimated <m>direction</m> of <m>gravity</m> from the <m>otolith</m> inputs to determine upright orientation.

Title: Gravity as a Strong Prior: Implications for Perception and Action
Abstract: Interestingly, there seem to be certain constraints as to when computations can access the internal <m>representation</m> of <m>gravity</m>; when the so called "<m>idiotropic</m> <m>vector</m>" along the vertical body axis, for example, is not aligned with the <m>direction</m> of <m>gravity</m>, the contribution of the internal <m>representation</m> of <m>gravity</m> decreases (De Sa Teixeira,; De Sa Teixeira and Hecht,).
